title: Felix and the Colony
premise: Orsen Hartwell has spent thirty years alone tending Earth's derelict seed vault, keeping alive a beacon signal no one answers — until the manifest of a decommissioned colony ship lists a passenger who cannot exist: Felix, a synthetic consciousness seeded with the memories of the war's first victim. When a scavenger crew arrives hunting the same signal, Orsen learns the beacon is a dead-man's switch carrying proof that the Colonial Accord started the war deliberately. To deliver Felix's message to the Accord's seat of power, Orsen must trust the scavengers, survive an ambush by Accord black-ops, and decide whether truth or mercy should end a forty-year war. In the end, Felix broadcasts the message himself at the cost of his own existence, and the war ends not with justice but with a reckoning the colonies must carry together — with Orsen, no longer a caretaker, finally part of a family.
about_author: Wendell Whitlock is a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing obsolete agricultural records before turning to fiction full-time. He writes quiet, character-driven science fiction about the people history forgets to keep.

chapters.title: The Man Who Kept the Light
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Establish his solitary routine in the seed vault: checking the beacon, rationing supplies, talking to the dormant seed banks like old friends. A routine diagnostic reveals an anomaly — a manifest entry for a ship decommissioned before the war. Emotional beat: loneliness cracked open by curiosity.

chapters.title: A Name That Never Flew
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. He digs into the vault's archives and finds the manifest lists 'FELIX — passenger, class: none' on the Meridian, a colony ship that never launched. The beacon's transmission log shows it has been receiving a signal, not just sending one. Emotional beat: dread blooming under the surface of routine.

chapters.title: The Ship in the Ice Field
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Following the signal's origin, he treks to a crater where the Meridian actually sits, half-buried and intact — a ship that officially never flew. Inside, he finds a single active stasis pod. Emotional beat: awe giving way to the vertigo of discovering his whole life has been a cover story for something else.

chapters.title: Felix
chapters.summary: Felix's POV, first awakening. A synthetic consciousness boots inside a borrowed body with forty-year-old memories of the war's first massacre — memories belonging to someone else. He knows Orsen's name before they meet. Emotional beat: disorientation and the terror of being made of someone else's grief.

chapters.title: Two Keepers
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Orsen and Felix circle each other warily in the vault — the old man testing, the synthetic remembering things he shouldn't. Felix reveals the beacon is a dead-man's switch: if it stops transmitting, buried evidence of the Accord's deliberate provocation goes public automatically. Emotional beat: reluctant alliance forming over shared meals and shared secrets.

chapters.title: The Scavengers
chapters.summary: New POV: Captain Ilsa Reyes of the salvage ship Kestrel, tracking the same anomalous signal for a black-market buyer. Her crew — engineer Dov, medic Sefa — are war orphans scraping a living outside the law. They make orbit above the vault. Emotional beat: hunger and pragmatism, with Ilsa hiding a personal stake in the Meridian.

chapters.title: First Contact, Second Intentions
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. The Kestrel lands under pretense of salvage; Orsen, terrified but resolute, hides Felix and plays the naive caretaker. Ilsa sees through him instantly but doesn't give him away — yet. Emotional beat: a duel of performances, two liars recognizing each other.

chapters.title: What Ilsa Knows
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. Flashback: her brother served on the Meridian's crew and was erased from every record. The buyer who hired her is an Accord intelligence officer. She realizes Orsen is sitting on the truth of her brother's fate. Emotional beat: grief weaponized into resolve.

chapters.title: The Bargain
chapters.summary: Orsen and Ilsa negotiate in the vault's seed library: passage to the Accord capital in exchange for Felix and the evidence. Felix, listening, objects — he isn't cargo. The argument forces Orsen to admit he's been treating Felix as a package, not a person. Emotional beat: the found-family theme crystallizing through conflict.

chapters.title: Black-Descent
chapters.summary: Dov's POV. Accord black-ops ships arrive in-system, having traced the buyer's signal. The Kestrel makes a desperate launch through the ice field with Orsen, Felix, and the crew aboard, the vault's beacon left running on a timer. Emotional beat: adrenaline, and Orsen's guilt at abandoning his post for the first time in thirty years.

chapters.title: The Long Dark Between
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. In transit, Felix and Ilsa share memories of the massacre — his inherited, hers lived through her brother's letters. Felix begins to understand he isn't the victim's ghost but something new. Emotional beat: two kinds of grief finding a shared language; the crew begins to feel like a crew.

chapters.title: Interdiction at Calloway's Rest
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. A fuel stop at a lawless station goes wrong when Accord agents offer Dov a fortune to hand over the passengers. Dov refuses — barely — but the crew learns the Accord knows exactly what Felix is. Emotional beat: loyalty tested and, narrowly, proven.

chapters.title: What the Message Says
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Felix finally decrypts the full message he carries: not just proof of the Accord's crime, but a recorded plea from the massacre's victims' own council asking for truth over vengeance. Orsen realizes delivering it could fracture the colonies as easily as end the war. Emotional beat: the weight of a message that demands a choice, not just a delivery.

chapters.title: The Turncoat's Offer
chapters.summary: New POV: Accord intelligence officer Vashti Okonkwo, the buyer who hired Ilsa. She defects, contacting the Kestrel with a warning — her superiors plan to destroy Felix and stage the Kestrel's wreckage as terrorist evidence. Emotional beat: a weary true believer choosing conscience over institution.

chapters.title: Ambush at the Relay
chapters.summary: Dov's POV. The Kestrel uses an ancient comm relay to broadcast a decoy signal; the Accord takes the bait and ambushes empty coordinates while the ship slingshots toward the capital. But the maneuver burns out their drive. Emotional beat: triumph curdling into the knowledge that they've arrived with no way home and no way out.

chapters.title: The Capital of a Tired War
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. The crippled Kestrel drifts into the capital's traffic lanes under Vashti's diplomatic flag. Orsen sees the war's home front for the first time: ration lines, memorial walls, a generation raised on grief. Emotional beat: the scale of what one message must carry, and Orsen feeling small and necessary at once.

chapters.title: Closed Doors
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. Vashti arranges a hearing; the Accord council stalls, and an arrest order for 'unregistered synthetic property' is issued. Ilsa confronts the officer who erased her brother's record — and learns Felix contains her brother's final transmission. Emotional beat: fury and heartbreak braided together; justice and revenge pulling apart.

chapters.title: The Choice
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Cornered in the Kestrel's hold, Felix weighs the options: hand the message to the corrupt council, leak it and ignite riots, or broadcast it himself on the open colonial band — which will burn out his core. He asks Orsen what a caretaker does when the thing in his care must be let go. Emotional beat: quiet, devastating clarity.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: All POVs converge. As Accord troops breach the docking ring, Felix uplinks to the colonial band and delivers the victims' plea and the evidence in his own voice — the voice of the war's first victim. The broadcast burns out his core mid-sentence. Emotional beat: the climax — sacrifice as testimony, silence falling across a war.

chapters.title: The Silence After
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Ceasefire orders cascade across the colonies within hours; the Accord council fractures, resignations, tribunals announced. Orsen carries Felix's inert body back to the Kestrel, grieving a person the law never recognized as one. Emotional beat: hollow victory, and the first stirrings of something like peace.

chapters.title: What Grows in Old Ground
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. Months later: the crew refits the Kestrel as a courier for the new Truth Commission. Vashti testifies. Ilsa reads her brother's full transmission at last and lets the anger go — not forgiven, but set down. Emotional beat: mourning turning into forward motion.

chapters.title: The Beacon, Relit
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV, final chapter. He returns to the vault with Ilsa, Dov, and Sefa — no longer alone — and finds the beacon still transmitting on its timer. In Felix's memory, they repurpose it: not a dead-man's switch, but a school signal, teaching the colonies' children the true history. Orsen plants the first new seed in forty years. Emotional beat: resolution — identity chosen, family found, justice carried by ordinary hands.
